replace.align_plan:
Answer, from inverse kinematics alone, which standoff poses facing one target from one named side an arm can actually hold.
Use when: you have a current target_ref and need an IK-only comparison of standoff poses from a named side. This is optional diagnosis, not a prerequisite for every approach. Near miss: this is not grasp_plan (where on this object do the fingers close); use grasp_plan for contact geometry and candidate finger poses; use move_pose when you already have the pose to command. An unreachable result describes this solver attempt, not an impossible approach side. If you later call grasp_plan, inspect its candidates independently: grasp_plan takes no approach_side or align candidate input, so it does not inherit this side selection. The five sides are world-frame directions toward the object and never toward an arm: top stands off above the target and travels down (world -Z), front stands off at -X travelling +X, back at +X travelling -X, left at +Y travelling -Y, and right at -Y travelling +Y. Choose the arm separately in arm; approach_side "left" does not mean the left arm. Two bounded numbers shape the request: standoff_m is the distance in metres from the target's visible-surface centroid to the candidate link6 position (default 0.10 m, permitted 0.02-0.30 m), and max_candidates is how many jaw rolls to sweep at that one position (default 3, at most 6).
Effect: read-only. No action is submitted, no world state changes, no artifact is written, and no observation is produced or consumed. Every candidate is solved by inverse kinematics from this arm's current measured joint configuration against its joint limits, so motion_planner_called is false in every result and the same request can answer differently after the arm has moved.
Returns: schema, the echoed target_ref, approach_side and requested_arm, motion_planner_called, and candidates. Each candidate carries source_index (which synthesised pose it came from, counting from 0), arm, align_pose = {position_m [x,y,z] in metres, orientation_xyzw [x,y,z,w] normalized} as a world-frame public link6 pose, reachable, position_error_m in metres and orientation_error_rad in radians at the best joint configuration the solver found, iterations (1 on this backend: one SDK IK solve per pose), rejection_reason (null when reachable; otherwise ik_failed when the SDK IK found no joint solution, ik_branch_jump when every valid solution needs a raw joint move larger than pi rad from the current configuration -- another arm branch the joint interpolation would sweep through -- or fk_residual_exceeded when a solution misses the pose by more than 0.01 m or 0.1 rad) and claim_boundary. All candidates share one standoff position and differ only by jaw roll about the approach axis. arm "both" returns one candidate per arm per pose, keyed by (arm, source_index). Unreachable candidates are returned rather than dropped, so a ruled-out side can be cited. Read position_error_m and orientation_error_rad rather than trusting the word reachable, then command a chosen align_pose through move_pose: under targets.<selected_arm>, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion and copy position_m and orientation_xyzw. Select interaction by physical intent. Schema example only; replace this illustrative pose and arm with your chosen current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
 There is no later receipt and no reference to resolve, because nothing was submitted.
Does not: prove that a collision-free path exists, plan or execute any motion, avoid the table, the target or anything else in the scene, or promise that move_pose to a returned pose will arrive. A returned pose has not been tried: reachable means only that this model of this arm admits a joint configuration holding that pose. It is not a grasp, not a contact, not retention and not task success, and it makes no claim about the gripper, which is neither commanded nor read. The standoff is measured from the visible-surface centroid of the segmented mask, not from the object's true centre, so an occluded or one-sided view biases every candidate toward the camera. An unreachable verdict describes this arm from its present configuration; it is not proof that the approach is impossible. Use position_error_m and orientation_error_rad to interpret this attempt; do not turn them into a probability of path feasibility. Only the motion tool attempts the actual route. On this backend this tool and the motion tools use the same SDK inverse-kinematics solve: 32 seeds from the current joints, this arm's own self-collision checked at the endpoint, and the straight joint interpolation screened for self-collision and against the other arm at its measured joints. It does not model objects on the table, the tabletop surface, finger links or a held payload. A pose reported reachable can still be refused by a motion that starts from a different measured configuration.
On error: invalid_arguments naming standoff_m means the value left 0.02-0.30 m -- resubmit inside that range instead of retrying the same number. invalid_arguments naming approach_side means the string is not one of the five declared directions; re-read this tool's approach_side enum and select one of its values rather than inventing a synonym. invalid_arguments naming arm means the name is not an arm of this embodiment; this tool's arm enum is the complete list of what it has. target_ref_unavailable means no such segmented target exists and stale_observation means the reference predates the current observation: re-run vision_segment or vision_ground on the current view and use the new reference. target_geometry_unavailable is retryable and means the mask or its depth is too poor to locate a centroid, so obtain a clearer current view of that target first. ik_branch_jump is not a joint limit: the pose is holdable only from another arm configuration, so prefer another jaw roll or side, or move the arm with recover_pose or a free-space move_pose toward that side and ask again. When candidates are unreachable, use their residuals and current geometry to choose a different side, standoff or arm if that answers a specific uncertainty. Do not exhaustively sweep unchanged requests. A world move changes the starting configuration and invalidates target references; obtain a fresh target before another query.
replace.move_to:
Move selected public link6 controlled points to world-frame positions while holding each measured action-start orientation. Use when: the intended change is translation-only free-space repositioning and a position-only trajectory label is useful. Effect: world mutation; compiles through canonical move_pose with interaction=free_space, so the Runtime solves one SDK inverse-kinematics target and interpolates the joints within the command's reserved window of at most 20 native actions, stopping at measured arrival; the route is screened for this arm's own self-collision, at the endpoint and along the straight joint interpolation, and against the other arm, not against objects, the tabletop, finger links or a held payload. Returns: the later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to select a controller implementation; rotate, command a gripper, infer contact intent, avoid obstacles, or guarantee reachability. On error: inspect the named failure stage and current residual, then choose a reachable intermediate or recover_pose after a genuine motion failure. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.move_pose:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public link6 controlled point to a stated position and orientation. Send one or both arms under targets; an omitted arm is not commanded. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in targets.<arm>. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name.
Effect: compiles the request once. It reserves up to 20 native actions of the task's native-action limit and stops at measured arrival. free_space always uses the global route: one SDK inverse-kinematics solve plus joint interpolation, screened for this arm's own self-collision at the endpoint and along the straight joint interpolation, and against the other arm (both arms together when one call moves both; no objects, tabletop, finger links or payload), with no trajectory planner; precision uses one bounded local Cartesian step when the complete change is within 50 mm and 15 degrees and the global route otherwise; contact_approach up to 50 mm/15 degrees is local, while a larger contact approach first reaches a pre-contact pose on the global route and locally executes only the final 40 mm/9.3 degrees. Small in-place rotations may be local. Every stage uses measured convergence and a local failure never silently falls back to global.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose the global versus local route; avoid obstacles; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: an argument refusal names the field and the bound it violated, never a branch index. position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at targets.<arm>.translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed means the bounded SDK inverse-kinematics solve admitted no joint target; plan_rejected means zero controller writes, including an inverse-kinematics branch jump (ik_branch_jump or local_ik_branch_jump) and workspace targets; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.recover_pose: Move selected arms to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving all gripper commands. Use when: a planner/execution failure or poor configuration makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to the joint configuration measured when that arm's most recent admitted pose action started, whether or not it arrived, and choose home for a deliberate return to the RoboDojo episode reset joints. Prefer one-arm recovery unless both arms genuinely require synchronized retreat. Effect: world mutation through the canonical recovery boundary; the stored joints are reached by joint interpolation with no planner, in a joint order screened for this arm's own self-collision and against the other arm (no objects, tabletop, finger links or held payload), omitted arms receive no drive target, and a recovery does not replace the saved previous configuration. Returns: the later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion and truthful unknown values; this backend measures no contact force. submitted public strategies and recovery mapping immediately; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual execution, residuals, preservation and drift. Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release a gripper, reverse an old trajectory, undo physics, act as an emergency stop, model scene or payload collisions, or guarantee escape from contact. On error: inspect each arm result and scene state, retry one arm at a time or use the other strategy only when physically sensible; stop and finish with failure or abort if both recovery routes are exhausted or unsafe.
replace.set_gripper:
Set one or both grippers to a named directive in a single call.
Use when: you are opening to release or approach, or closing to grasp, and you already know which directive each gripper should hold. On a two-armed embodiment this is how the two are coordinated: naming both in one call is the only way to state that they change together. Near miss: this is not grasp_execute. If you have chosen a current grasp candidate and accept the committed sequence without intermediate decisions, call that instead -- it approaches, closes and measures as one committed sequence, and a bare close here does none of that. Use this standalone command when a separate decision after pose execution is needed.
Effect: submits one gripper directive per named gripper through the Supervisor; an accepted command consumes one robot decision, and a refusal that executed no native actions and changed nothing consumes none. **An omitted gripper holds its current directive; it is not re-sent and not re-actuated.** The end-effector pose target is held unchanged. Measured state may still move under contact, and that is evidence rather than a fault.
Returns: a submitted acknowledgement, then a measured receipt and a fresh observation on the next turn. When closing, an intent block echoes the target_ref you supplied and labels it agent_annotation_only.
Does not: prove anything was grasped, held, released or moved; report jaw separation; verify what the jaws closed on; or make target_ref evidence -- it is your annotation of what you believe you are closing on, never a measurement. A closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: invalid_motion_arguments names the field that was wrong -- re-read this schema rather than resubmitting the same shape. invalid_arguments naming target_ref means a blank string was sent; send a non-empty reference or omit it entirely. Timing: one native action is 10 physics steps of 4 ms (25 Hz, 40 ms per native action), so one command's 20 native actions last at most 0.8 s. Under the SDK drive limiter the jaws travel at most about 0.16 of the opening per native action: a free-air close from fully open reaches the closed floor (normalized opening about 0.185) in about 6 native actions (0.24 s), and a free-air open from closed takes about 8 (0.32 s). A command ends as soon as every named gripper is within 0.03 of its effective target, or has stopped short of it: three consecutive native actions that each moved less than 0.005 of the normalized opening. A close that stops on an object therefore ends 3 native actions (0.12 s) after the jaws stop, and reports not_reached with failure_code gripper_stalled_before_target and, for each named arm, arms.<arm>.gripper_outcome: state, commanded_opening_normalized, effective_target_opening_normalized, measured_opening_normalized (both fingers' mean), sdk_limited_drive_target_normalized (0.2 below the first finger's reading while the jaws are held apart), measured_finger_displacements_m, finger_lateral_offset_m, primary_finger_limit_holds_close (true when the close stopped with the second finger at that held target), ticks_used, ticks_budget and seconds_used. That is the expected result of closing on an object, not a controller fault. gripper_not_reached with state moving_at_budget means a jaw was still moving when the 20 native actions ran out. A stalled close is consistent with a grasp but does not prove one, and the normalized opening is not a calibrated jaw width: lift and observe to check retention.
replace.grasp_execute:
Execute your selected grasp through open, pregrasp, approach, close, lift and verify.
Use when: grasp_plan returned candidates on the current observation and you selected one, the gripper may open at its current position, and a short upward probe is appropriate. Use manual motion for articulation or a grasp that must not lift.
Effect: opens the gripper first, which releases anything currently held; a nearly closed gripper is not proof it is empty. Moves to the candidate's pregrasp pose, follows its approach to the contact pose, closes, then requests 3 cm world-up at the same orientation. The Supervisor drives five stage actions as one robot decision with no intermediate Agent turn. Pose stages use the same semantic motion route as manual move_pose: free-space pregrasp, contact approach, and precision lift. Opening uses the embodiment's open directive, not the candidate's predicted aperture. Targets are committed once.
Returns: the submitted sequence and cost immediately; on the next turn, stage statuses, the post-close baseline images and current post-lift images, the measured link6 lift (this backend publishes no jaw separation: ARX finger readings are normalized encoder values, and the close stage's gripper_outcome and the verify stage's jaw_hold are the jaw evidence), plus rigid-versus-stationary depth support for the selected visible surface. Occluded, unavailable or ambiguous surface evidence is unknown.
Does not: change candidate, retry, stop for a decision halfway, infer an empty gripper before opening, or certify attachment, stable transport or task success. Depth support does not re-identify an object; a completed sequence only records execution.
On error: stale candidates require grasp_plan on the current observation. Missing geometry is refused before submission. A stage that does not arrive ends the sequence before later stages, with a fresh observation; inspect it and re-plan. If lift did not complete, the final scene may differ from the post-close baseline. Before opening or committing, runs one read-only backend probe for the selected exact pregrasp from the current measured joints. A refusal submits no action and reports grasp_pregrasp_unreachable with a bounded planning summary; select another candidate or reposition. Passing covers only this current-state pregrasp under the backend's published collision coverage. The Supervisor revalidates execution after opening; contact, lift and retention remain unchecked by the probe. The acknowledgement and final receipt include precommit_motion_check (one query, zero robot decisions). Its close stage uses the same jaw rule as set_gripper: a close that stops on the object ends 3 native actions after the jaws stop, the close stage reports status executed with reason gripper_stalled_before_target and a gripper_outcome measurement per closing arm, and the committed sequence continues to lift and verification; a stall is not a verified grasp. On this backend a refused probe's summary also carries ik_candidate_counts (SDK IK solutions returned, valid endpoints, and those within the joint-jump limit), ik_outcome_counts such as no_valid_endpoint, and constraint_rejection_counts per filter; they describe one bounded SDK IK solve, not proof that the pregrasp is unreachable.
replace.observe:
Inspect current or saved public camera images without moving the world.
Use when: you need named-point overlays or a saved same-round view, including the same camera's earlier view of an object you are checking for retention. Current physical-camera RGB and calibration are already delivered automatically; use those images directly when sufficient. Calling observe does not advance or recapture the world.
Effect: read-only; step selects an immutable observation in the current round, never recaptures or rewinds the environment.
Returns: images, dimensions and actual or actual_historical_observation status; historical results name observation_step.
Does not: establish object identity, attachment or task success; historical images are not the current world.
On error: choose a saved step in the current round. With step, use physical camera views only and omit history_point_ids. For a complementary retention check, inspect the same camera both at baseline and now, then segment each with its matching step. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured. Images are explicitly indexed when present. All current physical camera RGB and calibration are delivered automatically before decisions. Depth stays query-based; precise pixel measurements use mark_point. Omitted views selects every physical camera; request a subset only for a specific overlay or historical comparison. Public robot facts: return measured pose, controlled-frame world axes, and measured finger/command state with explicit semantics. Each returned physical camera includes native RGB dimensions, pinhole intrinsics and a world-to-camera CV transform from this exact observation; historical requests use historical calibration. Derived point-cloud panels have no pinhole calibration. Full current camera coverage is supplied automatically. Numerical joint opening alone never proves a grasp; unavailable measurements remain null or explicitly unavailable. Each calibrated camera also carries controlled_point_pixels and jaw_center_pixels per arm: the native OpenCV pixel [x, y], inside_image, in_front_of_camera and depth_m, computed from that camera's calibration and the measured pose of the same observation (automatic current delivery carries the same fields). The controlled point is the link6 wrist flange, which sits behind the arm's own wrist camera, so its wrist pixel is null. The jaw contact centre is the nominal pad contact centre 0.1501 m ahead of link6 along the approach axis; in the arm's own wrist camera it projects near the horizontal centre, below the image centre, not at it. Centring an object in a wrist view therefore does not put it between the jaws; compare the object with jaw_center_pixels instead. It is nominal source geometry, not a measured contact or grasp.

append.grasp_verify_retention: On this backend the closed interval comes from the public close directive in the command history, and the gripper motion compared is the measured link6 pose change applied as a rigid motion. No jaw width enters the comparison: ARX finger readings are normalized encoder values, not a calibrated aperture. The jaw evidence this backend does publish, a close that stops on an object and is reported as gripper_stalled_before_target with a gripper_outcome by set_gripper and by the grasp_execute close stage, is separate evidence to weigh beside this comparison; neither proves the object is held.
append.grasp_execute: On this backend each dispatched stage action is one robot command that reserves up to 20 native actions from the task's native-action allowance, so a complete sequence can consume up to 100.
append.place_execute: On this backend each dispatched stage action is one robot command that reserves up to 20 native actions from the task's native-action allowance, so a complete sequence can consume up to 80.
append.place_resume: On this backend each dispatched stage action is one robot command that reserves up to 20 native actions from the task's native-action allowance; the receipt's cost counts the stages dispatched.
